study type: Retrospective analysis of newborn screening data
outcome: False positive rate of newborn screening
Recognition of true-positive cases (e.g., methylmalonic acidemia with homocystinuria)
cohort: The study participants were over 37,000 newborns screened in the Italian Abruzzo region.
finding: Tailoring newborn screening with customized cut-offs reduced the percentage of newborns requiring second-tier tests to 1.47% (from an original 8%) while retaining the ability to recognize true-positive cases, suggesting enhanced precision medicine and reduced costs and analysis times.
cross-section timing: Newborn screening was performed shortly after birth.
